question.en: The genome-edited rice DRR Dhan 100, named Kamala, was edited from which parent variety?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 1 — Samba Mahsuri (BPT 5204)

India released the world's first genome-edited rice varieties in 2025. DRR Dhan 100 (Kamala) was produced at ICAR-IIRR, Hyderabad by editing the fine-grain favourite Samba Mahsuri (BPT 5204) so that it gives more grains per panicle and matures earlier.

The other variety, Pusa DST Rice 1, came from ICAR-IARI, New Delhi, which edited the DST (Drought and Salt Tolerance) gene in MTU 1010 for tolerance of drought and salinity.

Revision note — India's genome-edited rice

  • Both varieties were developed with CRISPR-Cas9 site-directed nuclease editing (SDN-1 and SDN-2), which leaves no foreign DNA, so they are not transgenic crops.
  • DRR Dhan 100 (Kamala) — ICAR-IIRR, Hyderabad; parent Samba Mahsuri (BPT 5204); edited for more grains per panicle and earlier maturity.
  • Pusa DST Rice 1 — ICAR-IARI, New Delhi; parent MTU 1010; edited for tolerance of drought and salinity.
  • ICAR was founded in 1929 as the Imperial Council of Agricultural Research; headquarters New Delhi; it works under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.
  • ICAR-IIRR carries the older name Directorate of Rice Research, which is where 'DRR' in the variety name comes from.
  • CRISPR-Cas9 won the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna.
  • Related releases to revise: India's first indigenous CRISPR-based gene therapy for sickle cell disease and the IISR Kozhikode turmeric variety.
  • Rice research institutes to keep apart: IIRR Hyderabad, NRRI Cuttack (formerly CRRI) and IARI New Delhi.

question.en: Which exception to the law of demand works through a dominant negative income effect?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 4 — Giffen goods

A Giffen good is a strongly inferior good on which a poor household spends a large share of its income. When its price falls the household is effectively richer and moves to better food, so demand falls as the price falls — the negative income effect outweighs the substitution effect.

It is named after Sir Robert Giffen, and its demand curve slopes upward. Veblen goods also slope upward, but through prestige, not income.

Revision note — law of demand and its exceptions

  • The law of demand: other things equal, a rise in price contracts the quantity demanded — an inverse relation.
  • It holds ceteris paribus — income, tastes, prices of related goods and expectations all unchanged.
  • Exceptions: Giffen goods, Veblen or conspicuous goods, speculation about future prices, necessities, emergencies and ignorance of quality.
  • A price change causes a movement along the demand curve; a change in income, tastes or related prices shifts the curve.
  • Demand for a normal good rises with income; for an inferior good it falls. Every Giffen good is inferior, but not every inferior good is Giffen.
  • Substitutes (tea and coffee) have positive cross elasticity; complements (car and petrol) have negative cross elasticity.
  • Price elasticity of demand = percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in price; demand is elastic when it exceeds 1.
  • Total revenue is maximised where elasticity equals one (unitary elastic).

Exception

Why demand rises with price

Giffen good

Negative income effect dominates for an inferior staple

Veblen good

The high price itself signals prestige

Speculation

Buyers expect the price to climb further

Necessity

The good must be bought at any price

Do not mix these up

  • Giffen is about income and poverty; Veblen is about status. Both break the law of demand, for opposite reasons.

Also asked from this topic: which option is NOT an exception to the law of demand (SSC Selection Post 2025 (Phase XIII)), what the law of demand says happens when price rises (Delhi Police Constable (Exe) 2025-26), and when total revenue is maximised in relation to elasticity (SSC CPO Paper-1 2025).

question.en:
Consider the following statements about the World Trade Organization.

I. It replaced the GATT, which had been in force since 1948.

II. It was set up by the Marrakesh Agreement that closed the Uruguay Round.

III. It works as a specialised agency of the United Nations.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 3 — I and II only

The GATT, signed in 1947 and in force from 1 January 1948, was replaced by the WTO on 1 January 1995, created by the Marrakesh Agreement of April 1994 at the close of the Uruguay Round (1986-94).

The WTO is not a specialised agency of the United Nations — unlike the IMF and the World Bank, it sits outside the UN system. Its headquarters is at Geneva, Switzerland.

Revision note — the WTO

  • Headquarters Geneva; 166 members; working languages English, French and Spanish.
  • India is a founder member from 1 January 1995, and had been a GATT contracting party since 1948.
  • The top decision-making body is the Ministerial Conference, which meets at least once every two years; the General Council runs day-to-day work.
  • Decisions are normally taken by consensus, on the principle of one member one vote.
  • Core agreements: GATT (goods), GATS (services), TRIPS (intellectual property), TRIMS (investment measures) and the Agreement on Agriculture.
  • The Agreement on Agriculture sorts subsidies into the Green, Amber and Blue boxes.
  • The Dispute Settlement Body decides trade disputes; its Appellate Body has been unable to function since 2019 for want of appointments.
  • The Director-General is Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, the first woman and the first African in the post.

question.en: Which of these industries was the first to be established in modern India?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 2 — Cotton textiles at Bombay

India's first successful cotton textile mill was set up at Bombay in 1854 by Cowasji Nanabhai Davar. The first jute mill followed a year later, at Rishra near Serampore in Bengal in 1855, under George Acland.

The first cement plant came only in 1904 at Madras, and TISCO's iron and steel works was set up at Sakchi, later Jamshedpur, in 1907. Cotton and jute are agro-based; cement and steel are mineral-based.

Revision note — classification of industries and India's industrial firsts

  • By raw material: agro-based (cotton, jute, sugar, paper, edible oil), mineral-based (iron and steel, cement, aluminium), forest-based and marine-based.
  • By size: micro, small, medium and large, classified under the MSMED Act on investment and turnover.
  • By ownership: public, private, joint and cooperative — AMUL is the standard cooperative example.
  • By role: a basic or key industry feeds other industries (iron and steel); a consumer goods industry serves users directly (sugar, toothpaste).
  • TISCO was conceived by Jamsetji Tata and established by his son Dorabji Tata in 1907, with steel production from 1912; an earlier attempt was the Porto Novo iron works in Tamil Nadu (1830).
  • The jute industry is concentrated in the Hugli basin of West Bengal; sugar, the second largest agro-based industry, in Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra.
  • The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 divided industries into three schedules and gave the public sector the commanding heights.
  • The 1991 policy abolished industrial licensing for most industries, keeping it for a short list of strategic sectors.

question.en:
Consider the following statements about youth programmes in India.

I. The National Youth Policy 2014 defines youth as persons aged 15 to 29.

II. Mera Yuva Bharat was set up in 2023 as an autonomous body.

III. Nehru Yuva Kendras were started in 1972 for rural youth.

Which of the above statements are correct?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 1 — I, II and III

The National Youth Policy 2014, launched in February 2014, replaced the policy of 2003 and narrowed the definition of youth from 13-35 years to 15-29 years, the band now used in official statistics.

Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) was approved in 2023 as an autonomous body under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, and the Nehru Yuva Kendras, started in 1972, remain the ministry's rural youth-club network.

Revision note — youth development in India

  • The nodal ministry is the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, whose youth wing runs NYKS and the National Service Scheme.
  • NYKS (Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan) became an autonomous organisation in 1987 and is among the world's largest grassroots youth bodies.
  • The National Service Scheme was launched in 1969, the Gandhi centenary year, with the motto 'Not Me, But You'.
  • National Youth Day is 12 January, the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda; International Youth Day is 12 August.
  • Rashtriya Yuva Sashaktikaran Karyakram (RYSK) is the umbrella covering NYKS, the National Youth Leadership Programme and youth hostels. NSS is a separate scheme.
  • MY Bharat was launched on 31 October 2023, Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, as a technology-driven platform for youth volunteering.
  • Census 2011 put the 15-29 age group at about 27.5% of India's population.
  • The earlier National Youth Policy 2003 had used the far wider band of 13 to 35 years.
